notes: Authoritative sources: Neat's official User Manual rear-panel diagram (cdn-stories.neat.no, rev03, 2024) and official Device Sheet (cdn-stories.neat.no, 2025), plus neat.no/bar-2 and us.neat.no/bar-2 product pages. Neat does not publish exact version/speed numbers for HDMI, USB-C, or Ethernet anywhere in its official materials (manual, device sheet, or product pages) — so no bandwidth "grade" could be confirmed for any port and none was set, per the instruction to omit grade when the spec doesn't state a version. Camera output caps at 1080p/30 for people video and 1080p/30 (or 720p/60) for content sharing, and the unit drives "up to two 4K screens," but this does not reliably indicate the HDMI output's cable-spec version (1.4 vs 2.0), so it was left unset rather than guessed. The AC power connection is a captive/internal-power-supply cord (100-240V~ 50/60Hz 0.5A) built into the unit — there is no exposed IEC/NEMA inlet; "dc-barrel" was chosen as the closest available connector id for this captive low-voltage supply cable, though physically it is a fixed cord rather than a barrel jack (caveat noted). A "USB-C Debug" port also appears on the rear-panel diagram (service use, not general AV I/O) and is included for completeness. Model is the standalone Neat Bar Gen 2 bar (SKU NEATBAR2-SE per us.neat.no schema metadata); it is typically paired with a separate Neat Pad touch controller (not included as physical ports here since Neat Pad is a distinct device with its own PoE/Ethernet I/O). No rack-mount option exists (desktop/wall/screen-mount device), so rackUnits is omitted. Confidence set to medium because manufacturer sources are authoritative and complete for port presence/names, but bandwidth grades could not be confirmed for any graded-connector-type port (HDMI, USB-C, Ethernet).
